findings.description: The 'data' bucket has no server-side encryption configured, so data stored at rest is not encrypted by default, exposing confidential data to anyone with access to the underlying storage.
The comment indicates the bucket is public, meaning it permits anonymous/unauthenticated access and exposes its contents to the entire internet.
The comments show the bucket does not have access logging enabled, eliminating the audit trail needed to detect unauthorized access to sensitive data.
Versioning is not enabled on the data bucket, so accidental or malicious deletion or overwrite of objects cannot be recovered.
This object stores 'customer-master.xlsx', a financial customer master file, in a bucket that is not encrypted and is public, exposing confidential customer data to the internet.
The 'financials' bucket has no server-side encryption configured, so financial data at rest is stored unencrypted.
The 'financials' bucket does not have access logging enabled, so there is no audit trail of access to sensitive financial data.
The 'operations' bucket has no server-side encryption configured, so operational data at rest is stored unencrypted.
The 'operations' bucket does not have access logging enabled, so there is no audit trail of access to its contents.
The 'data_science' bucket has no server-side encryption configured, so its data at rest is stored unencrypted.
force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contained objects to be deleted without protection, risking irreversible loss of the confidential customer master data on bucket destruction.
force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its financial data to be deleted without versioning protection, risking irreversible destruction of financial records.
force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its data to be deleted even though versioning is enabled, and combined with missing encryption it risks loss of sensitive operational data.
force_destroy = true permits deletion of the data science bucket and all its contents, risking irreversible loss of data science payloads.
The logs bucket uses acl = 'log-delivery-write', which grants the S3 log delivery group write permissions to the bucket, expanding the set of principals who can write to this bucket.
